title: finding(test-infra): `check-i18n-call-site-keys.test.ts`'s whole-corpus factory-drift test runs past the 15s default and times out under container load — a second instance of the class in #8062
body:
Same class as #8062, one file over. Related: #8062 — fold these into one card if triage prefers that; this one is filed rather than dropped because it is a second measured instance, on a different file, of a class that #8062 names only for `check-doc-links.test.ts`.

Observed while running the `scripts/__tests__/` directory as a gate for objectui#7850 (a change that touches neither this test nor anything it reads).

## The test

`scripts/__tests__/check-i18n-call-site-keys.test.ts`, in `a createSafeTranslation defaults row must repeat the en value too (objectui#7567)`:

    it('main carries no factory drift, over a surface big enough for that to mean something', ...)

Its own lead-in comment says what it walks: the whole `createSafeTranslation` corpus (the shipped measurement it records is 32 factories, hundreds of rows). It takes no `testTimeout` argument, so it runs against Vitest's 15000ms default.

## Three readings, same day, same tree

| Run | Load | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/` (112 files, 183.33s wall) | full directory in parallel | **timed out** — `Test timed out in 15000ms`, the case reported at 17450ms |
| `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/check-i18n-call-site-keys.test.ts` | file alone | exit 0, 130 passed, file duration 37.17s |
| `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/` (112 files, 124.70s wall) | full directory, lighter container | exit 0, 3344 passed |

So the case is not slow-and-broken and not fast-and-flaky: it sits close enough to the 15s line that whether it goes red is decided by how busy the box is when it runs. In a run where the whole directory takes 183s it is red; in one where the same directory takes 125s it is green. Nothing about the corpus changed between the two.

## Why it is worth a card

The failure mode is a gate that reds for a reason unrelated to what it measures. It costs an agent or a CI run a diagnosis pass that ends in "not mine", and — the sharper half — it trains readers to discount a red from this file, which is exactly the credit a drift gate needs to keep.

Not investigated here, and deliberately not prescribed: whether the remedy is a per-test `testTimeout`, a repo-wide default, splitting the corpus walk, or making the walk cheaper. #8062 raises the same question for its two cases, which is the main argument for one decision covering both.

Recorded by an agent seat while working objectui#7850, session `session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`. No code change was made for this observation, and it is out of scope for that card's pull request.
